title: Localized elementary devissage and neighbourhood transfer after further base changes
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finitely presented morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and let $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, $s=f(x)$, where $\mathcal F_s$ is the pullback to $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Support means nonzero stalks and $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$ uses dimension at a point [def-kun-dimension]. There exist an affine elementary etale neighbourhood $e:(S_1,s_1)\to(S,s)$, $A=\mathcal O_{S_1,s_1}$, affine $A$-schemes $X_1,Z,Y$, an elementary etale map $g:(X_1,x_1)\to(X_A,x_A)$, a finitely presented closed immersion $i:Z\to X_1$, a finite $A$-map $\pi:Z\to Y$, points $z\in Z$, $y\in Y$, and a finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal G$ on $Z$ with the following properties. Here $X_A=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$, $x_A$ is its point above $x$, $\mathcal F_A$ is the pullback, elementary means the marked residue-field map is an isomorphism, and $i(z)=x_1$, $\pi(z)=y$, $\pi^{-1}(y)=\{z\}$. The point $y$ lies over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s_1)$ is purely transcendental [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension]. The scheme $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ over $A$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically integral fibres (each fibre remains a nonzero integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] after every residue-field extension); $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is finitely presented; and $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F_A$. Write $\pi_*\mathcal G=\widetilde N$ and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ correspond to $y$. Then $N$ is a finite $B$-module, $A\to B$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $\mathcal F_x$ flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ implies $N_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] flat over $A$. Moreover, for every affine elementary etale neighbourhood $(T,t)$ of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, putting $C=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ and using subscript $C$ for base change, the marked fibres and residue fields of this diagram are unchanged, $g_C$ is etale, $i_C$ is a finitely presented closed immersion, $\pi_C$ is finite, $Y_C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is smooth with geometrically integral fibres of dimension $n$, and the canonical comparisons give $i_{C,*}\mathcal G_C\cong g_C^*\mathcal F_C$ and $(\pi_*\mathcal G)_C\cong\pi_{C,*}\mathcal G_C$. The following neighbourhood equivalences hold, also for $C=A$: $\mathcal F_C$ is finitely presented near the marked point of $X_C$ if and only if $\pi_{C,*}\mathcal G_C$ is finitely presented near the marked point of $Y_C$; and $\mathcal F_C$ is flat over $C$ near that point if and only if $\pi_{C,*}\mathcal G_C$ is flat over $C$ near its marked point. Flatness over a base, pullback, fibre products, residue fields, closed immersions, finite maps, and finite modules mean [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; etale is [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, elementary-devissage diagram and its localization, ending with reduction to smooth affines; returned steps 3, 4 and 11 (transfer of neighbourhoods)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-elementary-module-devissage] to $f,\mathcal F,x$. Its hypothesis that $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] holds: by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], for all affine opens $V\subseteq S$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ the ring map $\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ is of finite presentation, hence finitely generated by the images of its finitely many polynomial variables, and the affine opens $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ cover $f^{-1}(V)$. Obtain affine schemes $S_1,X',Z',Y'$, elementary pointed etale maps $e:S_1\to S$ and $g':X'\to X$, and $i',\pi',\mathcal G'$ with all six properties of that lemma. In particular $i'_*\mathcal G'\cong(g')^*\mathcal F$, $\pi'^{-1}(y')=\{z'\}$, and $Y'\to S_1$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ with geometrically integral fibres. Write $D=\Gamma(S_1,\mathcal O)$ and let $\mathfrak p$ represent $s_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A=D_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\kappa(s_1)=\kappa(s)$.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof: choose the diagram using Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage.

proof.text: The factorization $\bar g:X'\to X\times_S S_1$ is etale: both $X'\to X$ and $X\times_S S_1\to X$ are etale, so apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Base change $X',Z',Y',i',\pi',\mathcal G'$ along $D\to A$ to obtain $X_1,Z,Y,i,\pi,\mathcal G$. Affineness and the coordinate tensor-product descriptions follow from [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The base change of $\bar g$ is the required etale $g:X_1\to X_A$. The morphism $X\to S$ has a finite polynomial presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]; its base change does too by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Compose with the locally finitely presented etale $g$, using [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. Thus $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally finitely presented and, being between affines, finitely presented (the affine ring presentation gives this).

source.place: Tag 05I5, first proof: localization of the elementary-devissage diagram; Tag 05H2, lemma-etale-at-point; Morphisms Tags 02GO, 02GW, 01TR.

proof.text:
Handle the first localization and all the further changes at once. Let $R=A$, or let $R=C=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ as in the statement. In both cases the composite $D\to R$ is local at $\mathfrak p$ and induces the specified isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\kappa(R)$; for $C$ this uses exactly the elementary condition at $t$. If $W'$ is any of $X',Z',Y'$, then
$$(W'_R)_{\mathrm{closed}}=W'\times_{S_1}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(R)\cong W'\times_{S_1}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_1).$$
The same equality holds for the pulled-back modules, by the composition rule for module pullback. Thus the closed-fibre diagram, the marked points and their residue fields are identified with the original ones. This proves $i_R(z_R)=x_{1,R}$, $\pi_R(z_R)=y_R$, and $\pi_R^{-1}(y_R)=\{z_R\}$, since this entire last fibre is contained in the closed fibre. It also preserves $\kappa(y_R)/\kappa(R)$ and its pure transcendence. Likewise the closed fibre of $X_R$ is $X_s$, so there is a unique marked lift of $x$, the map $g_R$ induces the original residue-field isomorphism, and $\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)=n$ is unchanged. These are the fibre-product and pullback definitions [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback], applied to an isomorphism of residue fields; no field-extension invariance of dimension is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 05I5, first proof, base change to the local ring at s′; the closed-fibre identifications are written out from the definitions.

proof.text: For the same $R$, etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] gives $g_R$ etale, and finite base change [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] gives $\pi_R$ finite. A closed immersion of affine schemes is induced by a quotient, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write the coordinate map of $i'$ as $E\twoheadrightarrow H$. After tensoring, it is $E\otimes_D R\twoheadrightarrow H\otimes_D R$; its finite presentation is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition], so $i_R$ is a finitely presented closed immersion. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], $Y'_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$. For a point $r\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ mapping to $v\in S_1$ and any field extension $L/\kappa(r)$, its fibre extended to $L$ is $Y'_v\times_{\kappa(v)}\operatorname{Spec}L$, which is nonzero integral by the original geometrically integral fibre hypothesis. Hence all its fibres are geometrically integral. The finite presentation of $X_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ follows by base change of its affine polynomial presentation, as in step 2.

source.place: Tag 05I5, first proof, localized diagram; Morphisms Tags 02GO, 01WL, 01VB, 02NK, and Algebra Tag 05G5 for finite presentations.

proof.text:
The modules $\mathcal G_R$ remain quasi-coherent and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent, lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]. Since $i'$ and $\pi'$ are affine (a closed immersion is affine by its definition, and a finite map is affine), apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] to each of them. Pulling back $i'_*\mathcal G'\cong(g')^*\mathcal F$ and composing pullbacks gives
$$i_{R,*}\mathcal G_R\cong g_R^*\mathcal F_R.$$
Applying the same result to the localized $\pi$ and $A\to C$ gives precisely
$$(\pi_*\mathcal G)_C\cong\pi_{C,*}\mathcal G_C.$$
These are the canonical comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms: on affine coordinate modules they send $r\otimes m$ to $r\otimes m$, and the associativity identifications send $c\otimes(a\otimes m)$ to $ca\otimes m$. The cited base-change statement also supplies quasi-coherence of every pushforward here.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change, applied to the two affine maps in the diagram of Tag 05I5.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}H$, and $M=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal G)$. The affine finite-type criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] makes $M$ a finite $H$-module. The map $\pi$ is finite, so $H$ is a finite $B$-module by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. If $m_j$ generate $M$ over $H$ and $h_k$ generate $H$ over $B$, then $h_km_j$ generate $M$ over $B$: expand each coefficient in an expression $m=\sum_j a_jm_j$ in the $h_k$. Thus $N=M$, viewed over $B$, is finite and $\pi_*\mathcal G=\widetilde N$. Finally $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth, hence flat and locally finitely presented by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The affine presentation criterion gives $A\to B$ finitely presented, and [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion] applied to $\mathcal O_Y$ gives $B$ flat over $A$, using the stalkwise definition [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tag 05I5, first proof, reduction to the affine module N; Properties Tag 01PB and Morphisms Tags 01VE, 01VF.

proof.text: Suppose $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$. Apply the stalkwise assertion of [lem-trf-elementary-devissage-flatness] to the original diagram over $S_1$. It gives $(\pi'_*\mathcal G')_{y'}$ flat over $\mathcal O_{S_1,s_1}=A$. This is exactly $N_{\mathfrak q}$. Indeed write $B'=\Gamma(Y',\mathcal O)$ and $M'=\Gamma(Z',\mathcal G')$; then $B=(D\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B'$ and $N=(D\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}M'$ by step 5. Since $y'$ maps to $s_1$, every element of $D\setminus\mathfrak p$ is already invertible in $B'_{y'}$. Localizing once more at $\mathfrak q$ therefore gives $N_{\mathfrak q}=M'_{y'}=(\pi'_*\mathcal G')_{y'}$ with the same $A$-action. The local-ring localization is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], and [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization] identifies each actual module germ with localization of its affine section module. No flatness of the module away from the marked point is used.

source.place: Tag 057U, lemma-devissage-flat, stalkwise (a)⇔(c); Tag 05I5, first proof, base localization.

proof.text: Fix $R=A$ or $C$. Steps 2 through 5 exhibit elementary-devissage data over $\operatorname{Spec}R$: take the base neighbourhood to be the identity, the source neighbourhood to be $g_R:(X_{1,R},x_{1,R})\to(X_R,x_R)$, and use $Z_R,Y_R,\mathcal G_R$. The base identity and $g_R$ induce isomorphisms of marked residue fields by step 3. The closed fibre and its module support are the original ones, so the required integer is still $n$. All four auxiliary schemes are affine; $i_R$ is finitely presented, $\pi_R$ finite with the required singleton fibre, and $Y_R$ has the prescribed smoothness, dimension and geometric integrality. Moreover $X_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally finitely presented (step 4), hence locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] exactly as in step 1. Consequently the neighbourhood assertion of [lem-trf-elementary-devissage-finite-presentation] applies and gives the stated finite-presentation equivalence between $\mathcal F_R$ near $x_R$ and $\pi_{R,*}\mathcal G_R$ near $y_R$. Independently, the neighbourhood assertion of [lem-trf-elementary-devissage-flatness] gives the relative-flatness equivalence over $R$. Using step 5 to identify the pushforwards yields exactly both equivalences requested in the statement, including $R=A$.
